findings.suggestion: When a design hinges on loader revalidation/cookie semantics, a quick check of the framework-mode reference would turn the assumption into a verified fact; here it happened to be correct only because ssr:true.

findings.issue: Dependencies weren't installed until a typecheck chain failed with 'react-router: not found', burning one recovery turn.
findings.suggestion: Run `npm install` in app/ up front, as the spec itself instructs for build/start.

summary: A disciplined, front-loaded session: the agent read the entire spec, feature, codebase, test suite and fixtures before touching anything, designed a SSR-safe cookie+context architecture in its head, and implemented the whole feature in dependency order with zero rework or repetition. Its two real errors were small, self-inflicted and fixed in one step each from the error text. The main gap is verification: it stopped at typecheck plus a green test run and never looked at the rendered result, despite its own final-turn worries about SPA navigation.
